title: Home's model reads the request first, an unclear one is asked, and only a stated prediction shows the ML path
request: The owner tested Home twice and both chats went wrong: a vague request became a prediction and a segmentation request was asked what to measure before any table. The owner: understand people before routing them; AI first, rules as the fallback; later our own routing model first.
spec: Plan P0-P5 (~/.claude/plans/magical-waddling-honey.md): budget and failed readings said; the model reads first and the rules check; an open question before routing; segments and no column question before the data; every number checked; the page follows the kind of help.
plan: Model first, rules check, no silent default
Wait for the table before column questions
Fix the suites that relied on the default

decisions.decision: The model reads every request when Home has one; the rules run as a checker and alone only without a model
decisions.why: the sealed runs showed the rules overfit (0.78 dev, 0.72, then 0.58) while the model alone read 36 of 36; the owner's principle

decisions.decision: A clash between a strong rule reading and the model is asked in two buttons
decisions.why: code checks the model rather than silently choosing either

decisions.decision: Nothing read is an open question with all six kinds of help as buttons, never a prediction
decisions.why: the owner's first test: a vague request became a prediction with the ML workflow

decisions.decision: With no model, words that name a kind of prediction (a pack's own words, which ones will, a future) are read as one
decisions.why: the fallback must still serve clear prediction requests; about 40 suite tests showed what a pure ask would cost, and a vague request names none

decisions.decision: Segments get two ways: groups the person has (numbers per group) or a segmentation project with no outcome
decisions.why: both needs are real and only one of them is analysis; the engine already runs segmentation

decisions.decision: A brief question whose buttons come from the columns waits for the table
decisions.why: "What should I measure?" was asked with "Number of rows" as its only choice

decisions.decision: Every track's model reply has its numbers checked; on a prediction only the sentences with given numbers are kept
decisions.why: HOME-013's three uncited numbers came from the model's own examples on the prediction track, where the check was skipped

change: dclab_rnd/draft/intent.py (model-first read, rules as checker, open questions, failed readings, segments signal, the no-model kind-word fallback), dclab_rnd/draft/chat.py (ask_intent, the open-answer reading, the segments route, segmentation opening, checked_reply on every track, the pack cleared off prediction), dclab_rnd/draft/brief.py, dclab_rnd/draft/lang.py, dclab_rnd/prompts/home_intent.md and home_agent.md, dclab_rnd/agentic/web/src/views/home.html, tests.

findings.defect: A vague request became a prediction with the ML workflow and an outcome question
findings.scenario: "I have data analysis problems" on Home with Claude configured.
findings.cause: No rule matched; the model's reading was empty or failed and was swallowed; the reading fell to track prediction, source default, which the page called the usual start.
findings.fix: The model reads first; an empty, low-confidence or failed reading becomes an open question with every kind of help as a button; the failure is recorded as model_failed.

findings.defect: Customer segmentation was read as numbers and asked what to measure before any table
findings.scenario: "I want analyze my customer and segment of the my customer".
findings.cause: One rule ("analyze my") skipped the model; no track knew segments; the analysis brief asked its column-based field with no columns.
findings.fix: A segments signal (English and Persian) and its two ways; new groups open a segmentation project with no outcome question; column-based brief questions wait for the table.

findings.defect: Numbers nobody gave reached the person on the prediction track
findings.scenario: HOME-013: "1000" and "30" in model replies to prediction requests.
findings.cause: checked_reply returned early on the prediction track.
findings.fix: Every track is checked; the product's own example questions are allowed; on a prediction only sentences with given numbers are kept; the prompt forbids invented examples.

findings.defect: The segments rule read a column named segment in a join request as segmentation
findings.scenario: "Join the orders with the customer table ... city and segment."
findings.cause: The first rule matched the bare word segment.
findings.fix: The rule needs segmentation, clustering, personas, customer segments, or segments of a kind of row.

findings.defect: About 40 suite tests relied on unread requests becoming predictions
findings.scenario: The morning guard, journeys, fraud, team walks and coordinator suites with no model.
findings.cause: Their sentences name a prediction the intent rules do not read (fraud, which ones will, a future).
findings.fix: With no model, words naming a kind of prediction are read as one; tests whose vague sentence tests the prediction path start with the person's choice of a prediction.

findings.defect: With no model a bare future read as a prediction
findings.scenario: "I'm going to upload my customer table" and "What will help me with my data?".
findings.cause: The fallback's future pattern matched any "will" or "going to".
findings.fix: The fallback reads "will" only with an outcome (late, churn, buy, default and the like) and never "which" alone.

findings.defect: An edited sentence let the no-model fallback replace a model's reading
findings.scenario: The model read analysis; the person edited the sentence so a pack word appeared; replan moved the draft to a prediction.
findings.cause: The replan guard trusted source "rules"; the fallback is labelled rules too.
findings.fix: The fallback marks its reading (fallback: true) and replan never lets it replace a model's reading.

findings.defect: An answer typed after an either-or question was thrown away
findings.scenario: "Neither, I want a weekly dashboard" after a prediction-or-advice question.
findings.cause: The joined text was a new either-or (model reporting, rules prediction) and the branch started with the first old reading.
findings.fix: When the model reads the person's own answer it settles an either-or; the old reading is kept only for an open reading or the same pair again.

findings.defect: With no model weak words became the person's locked choice and a false label
findings.scenario: "not sure, maybe compare a few things" became a confirmed analysis by the user.
findings.cause: from_answer ranked any signal and its track was stored as the person's choice.
findings.fix: Only an exact button is the person's choice; words are read by the rules at their strong threshold, as a reading, not a choice.

findings.defect: The rules changed under their old version name
findings.scenario: The ledger's rule:intent_rules_v2 answers would mix two rule sets.
findings.cause: Segments and the fallback were added without a new version.

findings.defect: Open readings were never recorded, so the person's choice labelled nothing
findings.scenario: A vague request asked openly, then a button: intent_chosen(None, ...).
findings.cause: set_intent recorded only readings with a quote.
findings.fix: Asked readings are recorded too, so the choice labels them (routing data for the 7th model).

findings.defect: Segments depended on one regex and the answer on loose words
findings.scenario: The page's own chip got no signal; "I don't need new groups" started a segmentation project; a describe answer with no table got no reply.
findings.cause: Segments came only from a rules signal; the answer matched find/new/discover anywhere.
findings.fix: Groups of customers and behave alike in the rule, the model's need can mark segments, the buttons are matched first and a negation keeps the groups, and the next step is said when nothing is asked.

findings.defect: The memory said prediction while Home was asking
findings.scenario: An open reading has no track; memory.summary defaulted to prediction.
findings.fix: undecided while the kind of help is asked.

findings.defect: The business next step's "two periods" counted as an uncited 2
findings.cause: cited.numbers reads number words; the grader does not take Home's next-step texts as a source.
findings.fix: The next step says "the periods you name"; a test holds that Home's fixed texts carry no number.

findings.defect: The eval's Home-with-Claude arm never gave Home its intent reader
findings.scenario: HOME-015 (sealed v3): the rules and the model arm read the kind of help identically, 27 of 36 each; replayed afterwards with the reader, every failed request was read correctly.
findings.cause: agent_eval.home.observe built HomeAgent with the conversation's model only; the product (draft.work) also passes the home_intent client.
findings.fix: observe and measure take intent_for, and the runner's budget gives a home_intent client per draft; the counting wrapper passes the exchange id through.

findings.defect: A person who answered not sure to everything was asked seven times and never routed
findings.scenario: HOME-015: six requests with seven questions each.
findings.cause: After the buttons-only question an unclear answer asked the same question again.
findings.fix: After it, Home starts with its best reading (said, changeable) or stops asking and waits for the person.

measurements.name: The owner's two sentences on the real page, no model
measurements.gate: no ML panel; an open question or the segments route
measurements.result: an open question with six buttons; the segments route with two ways; workflow, outcome panel, pack and build hidden

measurements.name: Live replay with Claude of the owner's two sentences and one more (written, not the sealed set)
measurements.gate: no failed request; the right kind of help; no ML question off a prediction
measurements.result: an open question then analysis from the person's answer; analysis with the segments offer; a business question; EUR 0.019 in total

measurements.name: Thinking summaries by effort, claude-sonnet-5-5, three home_intent requests
measurements.gate: a summary on every call (the owner's rule)
measurements.result: 0 of 3 at the default, medium and high; 3 of 3 at xhigh (about 2.5 times a call's cost) and max; DCLAB_THINKING_EFFORT=xhigh set

measurements.name: Home sealed v3 (HOME-015), home_gate_v3
measurements.result: FAIL: the kind of help 27 of 36 in both the rules and the model arm (the model arm lacked the intent reader), English 0.92, Persian 0.38; one uncited number; the missing-column trap missed by every arm; Claude alone 36 of 36

outcome: Home asks before it routes and its model reads first; dev and a fresh sealed set are still to be measured.
lessons: A default that guesses hides itself in every suite that grew up beside it: changing it shows how many tests encoded the guess.
Rules tuned on dev sentences read the dev sentences; the reading belongs to the model, the checking to code.
Adaptive thinking decides for itself whether to think: asking for a summary is not enough to get one on short requests; the effort level is what makes it think.
An eval arm must build the agent the way the product does: a missing client measures a different system, and the numbers look plausible.
risks: The no-model fallback still reads some vague requests as predictions when they say a pack's word (a review, a ticket).
Not yet measured live on dev or a sealed set.
